results.name: CategoryTheory.SemiadditiveOfBinaryBiproducts.add_eq_left_addition
results.source_text:
theorem add_eq_left_addition (f g : X ⟶ Y) : f + g = biprod.lift f g ≫ biprod.desc (𝟙 Y) (𝟙 Y) :=
  congr_fun₂ (EckmannHilton.mul (isUnital_leftAdd X Y) (isUnital_rightAdd X Y) (distrib X Y)).symm f
    g

results.name: HahnSeries
results.source_text:
/-- If `Γ` is linearly ordered and `R` has zero, then `R⟦Γ⟧` consists of
  formal series over `Γ` with coefficients in `R`, whose supports are well-founded. -/
@[ext]
structure HahnSeries (Γ : Type*) (R : Type*) [PartialOrder Γ] [Zero R] where
  /-- The coefficient function of a Hahn Series. -/
  coeff : Γ → R
  isPWO_support' : (Function.support coeff).IsPWO
results.docstring:
If `Γ` is linearly ordered and `R` has zero, then `R⟦Γ⟧` consists of
formal series over `Γ` with coefficients in `R`, whose supports are well-founded.

results.name: CategoryTheory.SemiadditiveOfBinaryBiproducts.add_eq_right_addition
results.source_text:
theorem add_eq_right_addition (f g : X ⟶ Y) : f + g = biprod.lift (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X) ≫ biprod.desc f g :=
  rfl

instance (d : Dimension) (M : Type) [AddCommSemigroup M] :
    AddCommSemigroup (WithDim d M) where
  add_comm m1 m2 := by
    ext
    simp [add_comm]

/-- Given two maps `s1` and `s2` whose targets carry an instance of an additive commutative
  monoid, the target of the sum of these two maps also carry an instance thereof. -/
instance : (i : ι1 ⊕ ι2) → AddCommMonoid ((fun i => Sum.elim s1 s2 i) i) := fun i =>
  match i with
  | Sum.inl i => inst1 i
  | Sum.inr i => inst2 i

theorem eval₂_root (f : R[X]) : f.eval₂ (of f) (root f) = 0 := by

AdjoinRoot.isRoot_root
results.source_text:
theorem isRoot_root (f : R[X]) : IsRoot (f.map (of f)) (root f) := by

results.name: AdjoinRoot
results.source_text:
/-- Adjoin a root of a polynomial `f` to a commutative ring `R`. We define the new ring
as the quotient of `R[X]` by the principal ideal generated by `f`. -/
def AdjoinRoot [CommRing R] (f : R[X]) : Type _ :=
  Polynomial R ⧸ (span {f} : Ideal R[X])
results.docstring:
Adjoin a root of a polynomial `f` to a commutative ring `R`. We define the new ring
as the quotient of `R[X]` by the principal ideal generated by `f`.

results.name: Polynomial.eval₂_pow
results.source_text:
theorem eval₂_pow (n : ℕ) : (p ^ n).eval₂ f x = p.eval₂ f x ^ n :=
  (eval₂RingHom _ _).map_pow _ _

results.name: MvPolynomial.eval₂_pow
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem eval₂_pow {p : MvPolynomial σ R} : ∀ {n : ℕ}, (p ^ n).eval₂ f g = p.eval₂ f g ^ n
  | 0 => by
    rw [pow_zero, pow_zero]
    exact eval₂_one _ _
  | n + 1 => by rw [pow_add, pow_one, pow_add, pow_one, eval₂_mul, eval₂_pow]

/-- `MvPolynomial.eval₂` as a `RingHom`. -/
def eval₂Hom (f : R →+* S₁) (g : σ → S₁) : MvPolynomial σ R →+* S₁ where
  toFun := eval₂ f g

results.name: Polynomial.eval₂_pow'
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem eval₂_pow' (n : ℕ) :
    (p ^ n).eval₂ (algebraMap R S) x = (p.eval₂ (algebraMap R S) x) ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp only [pow_zero, eval₂_one]
  | succ n ih => rw [pow_succ, pow_succ, eval₂_mul', ih]

results.name: Polynomial.evalEval_pow
results.source_text:
@[simp]
lemma evalEval_pow (x y : R) (p : R[X][Y]) (n : ℕ) : (p ^ n).evalEval x y = p.evalEval x y ^ n := by
  simp only [evalEval, eval_pow]

results.name: Polynomial.eval₂
results.source_text:
/-- Evaluate a polynomial `p` given a ring hom `f` from the scalar ring
  to the target and a value `x` for the variable in the target -/
irreducible_def eval₂ (p : R[X]) : S :=
  p.sum fun e a => f a * x ^ e
results.docstring:
Evaluate a polynomial `p` given a ring hom `f` from the scalar ring
to the target and a value `x` for the variable in the target

results.name: Physlib.physHermite_pow
results.source_text:
lemma physHermite_pow (n m : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : physHermite n x ^ m = aeval x (physHermite n ^ m) := by
  simp

results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem eval₂_one : (1 : R[X]).eval₂ f x = 1 := by rw [← C_1, eval₂_C, f.map_one]

results.name: Polynomial.eval₂_at_one
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem eval₂_at_one {S : Type*} [Semiring S] (f : R →+* S) : p.eval₂ f 1 = f (p.eval 1) := by
  convert! eval₂_at_apply (p := p) f 1
  simp

results.name: Polynomial.evalEval
results.source_text:
/-- `evalEval x y p` is the evaluation `p(x,y)` of a two-variable polynomial `p : R[X][Y]`. -/
abbrev evalEval (x y : R) (p : R[X][Y]) : R := eval x (eval (C y) p)
results.docstring: `evalEval x y p` is the evaluation `p(x,y)` of a two-variable polynomial `p : R[X][Y]`.

results.name: Polynomial.evalEval_C
results.source_text:
lemma evalEval_C (x y : R) (p : R[X]) : (C p).evalEval x y = p.eval x := by
  rw [evalEval, eval_C]
